controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where TESS saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · July and August 2022, mapped in this project
controls.notes: TYC 486-4943-1 in its own color, darker where its light in TESS's images of July and August 2022 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 3.78 days its light rose and fell by 3.2%. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 12.9% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · TESS mission light curve, sector 54
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in TESS sector 54, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 3.2% as it turned once in 3.78 days. The light curve is the mission's own; the criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) decide that it shows the star turning, and starry finds the map that reproduces it. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 75°.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter. Black line: 75° S; the star never shows us what lies below it.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from Gaia's spectrum of the star; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,663 K and log g 4.64 (u1 0.743, u2 0.047): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.

controls.label: Radial field
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · CFHT ESPaDOnS spectra, Jun 2013
controls.notes: The star's large-scale magnetic field in Jun 2013, reconstructed in this project from 15 archived ESPaDOnS spectra with the published codes LSDpy and ZDIpy. It is this project's reduction, not a published map. Folsom, C. P. et al., arXiv:1601.00684 map the same run with a mean field of 25 G; this map has 12 G.
controls.legendNote: Red: field pointing out of the star; blue: into it. Black line: 75° S; the star never shows us what lies below it.
